edition.notes: An unattributed English translation of the complete constitution on a private aggregation site; no translator, source edition, or Latin text is named on the page, and the page's own date line reads only 'in the year 1738 of Our Lord' without day or month. The page carries injected third-party advertising text ('Read more: slot gacor') unrelated to the document, a witness-quality defect recorded here because it shows the delivery is not editorially controlled. The Latin original in the Bullarium remains the authoritative text; it was not collated for this record.

passages.context: The complete translation was read: the description of societies 'called in the popular tongue Liberi Muratori or Francs Massons' joining 'men of any Religion or sect' under 'a strict and unbreakable bond' with 'an oath upon the Holy Bible' to 'an inviolable silence'; the grounds ('For if they were not doing evil they would not have so great a hatred of the light', the harm 'not only to the peace of the temporal state but also to the well-being of souls', and 'other just and reasonable motives known to Us'); the condemnation and prohibition clause; the comprehensive membership and assistance prohibition 'under pain of excommunication ... incurred by the very deed without any declaration being required', absolution reserved to the Roman Pontiff except at the hour of death; and the direction that ordinaries and inquisitors proceed against transgressors 'as being most suspect of heresy'. The translation contains no allegation of devil-worship or of a specific secret doctrine; that bounded observation about this delivery is recorded with its limits in the consuming publication's research records.

alternate_titles: Constitution condemning the society of Liberi Muratori or Freemasons
work.author: Pope Clement XII
work.description: Clement XII's constitution of 28 April 1738, the first papal condemnation of the Masonic lodges: it condemns and prohibits the societies of Liberi Muratori or Francs Massons, forbids the faithful every form of membership or assistance under pain of an ipso facto excommunication whose absolution (outside danger of death) is reserved to the Roman Pontiff, and directs ordinaries and inquisitors to proceed against transgressors as suspect of heresy. Gasparri's fontes to canon 2335 of the 1917 Code cite it as litt. ap. In eminenti, 28 apr. 1738.
work.title: In eminenti apostolatus specula
